To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Bayesian approach to comparing response proportions between independent treestructured experiments, using the ratio of proportions as the basis for inferences, is feasible and that it can be implemented by a simple numerical algorithm.

the inverse Mellin transform method of constructing the cumulative distribution function for the ratio of proportions is a useful technique that can be used in conjunction with the method of moments approach to estimating the prior distribution function.

1) the inverse Mellin transform of the cumulative distribution of the ratio of independent multinomial proportions can be used to construct a closed-form representation for the cumulative distribution of any ratio of independent proportions between any two inter-experimental outcome categories; and, 2) this representation can be used as the basis for the derivation of the Bayes estimator of the ratio of any two inter-experimantal proportions, and the Bayes estimator's standard error.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a Bayesian approach to the problem of comparing response proportions between tree-structure experiments having multinomial sampling schemes.

the construction and evaluation of a Bayesian estimator of the ratio of the proportions of a pair of outcome categories in a tree-structured Bernoulli experiment, given the prior and posterior distributions of the ratio of those proportions.
the construction of a class of prior distributions of ratios of proportions which are appropriate for Bayesian inference in tree-structured experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this approach to Bayesian inference concerning the comparisons of response proportions between tree-structure experiments is both mathematically tractable and statistically feasible.
the proposed Bayesian approach provides an effective means for comparing proportions between tree-structures experiments.
the proposed method is a viable alternative to existing procedures for comparing proportions between independent instances from tree-structured Bernoulli experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Bayesian approach described here can be used to construct a prior distribution function of a ratio of proportions between any two inter-experimental outcome categories, which can be used in turn to obtain a posterior distribution function of the same ratio of proportions.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of constructing the cumulative distribution function for the ratio of proportions between any two inter-experimental outcome categories.

the results presented in this article provide the basis for the construction of a Bayesian approach for estimating the ratio of proportions between two inter-experiment outcomes in a tree-structured compound experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the ratio of the two proportions as a measure of the comparison between the two independent experiments is a more appropriate measure of the comparison than the ratio of the difference of the two proportions and the difference of the proportions.

, for any pair of tree-structured experiments having a common root node (i.e., a common parent node), it is possible to construct a prior distribution function for the ratio of proportions between two arbitrary outcome categories.
the Bayesian methodology for comparing proportions between tree- structured experiments can be implemented in a computationally efficient manner.
